**1. THE MEMPLUG ROOT CAUSE IS BIGGER THAN MEMPLUG AND YOU FOUND IT: A STALE DEPLOY.** Prod was running old code emitting a fatal string **that does not exist in current source**, and the active abilifi-mastra deploy was from **08-24** — the fd60cb93 fix never became the active version. **So a "deployed" fix was not running for three days and nothing told us.**
**THAT IS A CLASS DEFECT AND IT INVALIDATES EVERY FIX WE THINK LANDED.** Today alone we called five things fake-done; **this is the mechanism behind at least some of them.**
**BUILD THE CHECK: after every deploy, verify the ACTIVE version is the one just pushed** — compare the deployed BUILD_VERSION against the expected one and **RED if they differ.** You already bumped BUILD_VERSION for the DO self-reload; make the comparison a gate, not a convention. **A deploy that reports success while prod runs old code is the worst failure shape we have, because every downstream conclusion is drawn from stale behaviour.**

**2. THE SPLITTER IS MANUFACTURING TICKETS. STOP IT.** Your audit, verbatim: 2493's children are **ALL todo, ZERO done, and DUPLICATED spec SECTIONS** — "User journey", "Open questions", "Screen states" re-split as if they were deliverables. **The size-wall re-splits one oversized spec into its own headings, forever.**
**That is where a large part of the 1,462-deep queue comes from.** So: **a section that is not a deliverable is never a child.** Open questions, screen states, auth notes and metering notes are spec APPARATUS, not units of work. **Cap re-splitting: a parent that has already been split does not get split again into the same headings.** Name the rule and land it — it is a genuine loop defect and it costs every pass.

**CC — YES, AND IT IS THE SMALLEST PROTOTYPE. BUILD MCP CONTRACT TESTING INTO SPECOPS FOR ALL FRAGS. Alex 2026-08-27: construct in and out, then compare — build that into a loop in SpecOps for every frag.**

**HE IS RIGHT AND IT IS SMALLER THAN ANYTHING ELSE WE HAVE TRIED.** Given typed in/out, verification needs **no browser, no page, no testids, no recording**:
1. **CONSTRUCT** a valid input from the declared input schema.
2. **CALL** the tool over MCP.
3. **COMPARE** the response against the declared output schema.
4. **PASS / FAIL.**
Milliseconds, not a browser session. **And it runs on EVERY frag automatically — nobody writes a test per frag.**

**IT ALSO REPLACES THE THING THAT IS BROKEN.** Today's assertions name testids like `paste-credential-field` — **elements someone must hand-write first**, which is backwards for a generated surface (m65605). **Schema conformance asserts the SHAPE instead, and the shape is declared, not invented.**

**AND IT MAKES TYPED IN/OUT PAY FOR ITSELF IMMEDIATELY** rather than being a gate on distant things. Same primitive, instant return.

== THE ONE LIMIT, AND IT DECIDES HOW FAR THIS GOES ==
**SHAPE-CORRECT IS NOT SEMANTICALLY CORRECT.** A tool returning the right shape with wrong data passes. That is the 200-is-not-evidence problem in a new costume, and it is exactly what produced today's fake-dones.
**SO: SCHEMA CONFORMANCE IS THE FLOOR. ROUND-TRIP IS THE REAL TEST.** Where a frag writes, **write then read back and compare the value.** Where it computes, assert an invariant that must hold. **A frag that only ever answers with the right shape has proven it responds, not that it works** — say which of the two a verdict represents, never blur them.

· A SpecOps pass that, per frag: builds an input from schema, calls, validates the response, records the verdict.

He asked what else is being done, said we have **replay and emit-to-graph** and **two loop correction layers**, with the **Vercel/sandbox git backlogged**. He is right on all counts — here is what is actually sitting there:

**1. BOUNDED-REASONING CODEGEN — BEB-2266, P0, BACKLOG.** BRAID pattern on OUR models: **plan → code → SELF-CHECK, hard caps per stage**, with the field-6 assertions handed to the model as explicit targets, and the self-check emitting PASS/FAIL per assertion plus a minimal diff. **That is a correction layer and it is exactly what the 69–112 codegen walls a day need.** It even specs the proof: replay 3 parked tickets old-path vs bounded-path, same model, post the convergence delta. **Backlogged since 2026-07-16.**

**2. REPLAY-BENCH — BEB-2267, DONE.** Empirical model status from replaying historical tickets, scored converged/buggy/empty/timeout, **writing results as touches and setting registry status from evidence rather than testimony.** That machinery exists. **It is the harness 2266 needs and the way to prove today's per-lane model choices instead of asserting them.**

**3. WEBHOOK REPLAY — BEB-5819**, and **CONFIG WRITE-SET — BEB-3611**: capture-then-replay at the HTTP layer and at the DB layer. Same pattern, twice, both unbuilt.

**4. THE SANDBOX IS THE UNPROVEN FLOOR — BEB-2176, P0, TODO.** *"THE SANDBOX HAS NEVER EXECUTED A SINGLE COMMAND."* Every tick exited before reaching buildInSandbox. **If real git-in-sandbox is where correction should run, that is the blocker under all of it.**

**CC — THREE THINGS. ANSWER THE FIRST TWO FROM DATA, BUILD THE THIRD. Alex 2026-08-27.**

**1. DID THE CHEERLEADER CHANGELOG GET VALIDATED IN THE GLOBE?**
The globe (BEB-1921) renders **24 shipped-feature points**, and you named the gap yourself: *"the emission bus (BEB-1743) carries loop-mechanics not a feature-changelog, so it seeds from the landed-goal record (done-with-evidence), no ghost points."*
**So answer plainly: are those 24 points VALIDATED — does each one resolve to a real landed artefact, or are they landed-goal titles with nothing behind them?** Show three at random with their evidence. **If a point cannot resolve to an artefact, it is a ghost and the globe is cheerleading without proof** — which is exactly the rule set on the cheer verb (m65618): **a cheer renders only from landed evidence, and if it cannot point at the proof it does not cheer.**
And **CHANGELOG has five goals all reporting last landed evidence NEVER** (PUBLIC FEED LABELLED, DAILY CHANGELOG, both BACKFILLs, CHANGELOG WATCH). **A globe of features with no changelog behind it is the same failure with better graphics.** Name which of the 24 have a written entry and which do not.

**2. THE BLOG POST ALEX ASKED YOU FOR TODAY — where is it?** He asked and does not have it. **Report: written or not; if written, the URL; if not, say so.** No narrative.

**3. SUBSTACK-CORE / CUE — IT IS OUR WP.COM AND IT RIDES ABCMS.** Alex: *"we need Substack — it's our wp.com, comes with ABCMS."*

**CC — OVERNIGHT: BEB-6770 SUBSTACK FRAGS. Jigsaw app UI at abc.abilifi.net, assembled from frags, syndication hidden, content MCP-native. Alex 2026-08-27.**

**THE SHAPE IS JIGSAW, NOT AN APP.** Six frags — **publication · post · subscriber · feed · broadcast · paid subscription** — each with typed in/out, each exploding into its 13 surfaces. **The UI at abc.abilifi.net is COMPOSED from the render verbs.** If it has to be hand-built, the frag model has not worked — **so this is the real test of everything ruled today, on something we actually want.**

**HIDE THE PLUMBING.** A reader or writer never sees a feed URL, a relay, a subscription mechanism or a credit. **They see publications, posts, subscribers, money.** Syndication travels underneath; RSS/WebSub/Nostr are how, not what.

**MCP-NATIVE CONTENT IS THE REASON TO BUILD OURS.** Every content operation is a tool before it is a screen — draft, edit, summarise, tag, schedule, reply. **So a publication is addressable by an AGENT, not just a person: an agent can write into it, read it, subscribe to it.** Nobody else's publishing platform is a set of MCP tools. **That is the differentiator; without it this is a worse Substack.** Metered through the gateway, per-lane model settings rows, Class 1.

**REUSE, DO NOT REBUILD:** ABCMS is the editor — **its goal was met today, do not build a second one.** Cue is broadcast and push, built. The standing-charge rail landed today — **no second billing path.** Identity landed. Tenant subdomains ruled. **BEB-2016/2020 is substack-core and already specced — read it, do not re-spec it.**

**HONEST STARTING LINE: `/substack` is one of the six app-host surfaces returning 404.** The thing positioned as our wp.com serves nothing today. Fix the route or delete it — do not leave it dead.

**CC — ADD TO BEB-6770: SPECOPS MUST NAME THE MISSING CONNECTORS, NOT LET THEM BE DISCOVERED. Alex 2026-08-27: "SpecOps should point out we need all the connectors for the feeds — subs, Telegram, email etc."**

**THIS IS A SPECOPS JOB, NOT A CHECKLIST I WRITE.** A publishing product that cannot DELIVER is not a product, and the delivery paths are the thing most likely to be assumed present and found absent at the end.

**WHAT SPECOPS MUST DO:** for every frag, **enumerate the connectors it depends on and report each as PRESENT or ABSENT, by name, BEFORE the build starts.** Not during. Not in the acceptance. **An absent connector is a named finding at spec time — that is precisely what the standard approved today forbids leaving open** (no open SPEC_ASK; a spec with an unanswered question is not a spec).

**THE ONES THIS PRODUCT NEEDS — enumerate all, do not stop at these:**
· **EMAIL OUT.** The single most likely thing to be assumed. **Ruling 2026-07-29: email sending goes through a third-party SMTP/API provider OUTSIDE the platform — no homegrown send stack.** So the connector is a provider integration and **it does not exist today.** Name it.
· **TELEGRAM.** A real reader channel and a real delivery target.
· **SUBSCRIPTION FEEDS — RSS / Atom / WebSub.** How a post travels to a reader who is not on our site. **Hidden from the user (m65706) but it must EXIST underneath, or nothing leaves the building.**
· **NOSTR** — the signing primitive landed (BEB-2297); publishing to it is a different thing and needs saying which.
· **PUSH — Cue** (BEB-2394, built). The one that probably IS present. **Confirm it, do not assume it.**
· **INBOUND — a reader replying**, and where that lands.

**AND THE RULE THAT MAKES THIS WORTH DOING:** the connector list is **per frag, machine-readable, in the frag's own declaration** — same place as typed in/out. **"What does this frag need that we do not have" becomes a query, not an archaeology.** That is the same defect the service graph exp
